questions.prompt_en: Some people say university education should be free for everyone, while others believe students should pay part of the cost. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

answer.model_en:
The cost of higher education raises questions about fairness and public spending. Some people argue that university should be free to all students, whereas others believe learners should contribute financially. Both positions have reasonable arguments, but I favour a system in which public funding is combined with support based on need.
Those who support free university education point out that society benefits from a well-educated population. Teachers, engineers and healthcare professionals provide services that other people rely on. If tuition fees are very high, capable students from low-income families may avoid applying because they fear debt. Removing fees could make higher education more accessible and encourage people to pursue qualifications that are important to the community.
On the other hand, universities need substantial funding for staff, laboratories, libraries and student support. If all students attend for free, the government must meet these costs through taxation or reductions in other services. Some people therefore believe that graduates, who may earn more over their working lives, should contribute to the expense. This approach can be reasonable when repayments depend on income and do not place an excessive burden on new graduates.
In my view, the best policy combines public investment with carefully designed student contributions. Scholarships and living-cost grants should protect learners whose families cannot afford higher education. At the same time, any repayment system should be transparent and flexible enough to account for different incomes.
To conclude, free education may improve access, while student contributions can help universities remain financially sustainable. A mixed system with strong protection for disadvantaged students is more convincing than applying one rule to everyone.
